title: Starter
brief: Write a literary story told across seven mornings, one paragraph-cluster per morning, in which a woman keeps alive the sourdough starter her estranged brother left behind when he moved away. The brother never appears. The starter is not a metaphor anyone states aloud.
worldBible: The starter lives in a chipped blue jar labelled "Gus" in the brother's handwriting.
It must be fed flour and water every morning.
The brother moved to another country and has not called.
The story spans exactly seven consecutive mornings, Monday to Sunday.
She bakes only once, on the last morning.

contradicts: \bSami (?:walked in|knocked|arrived|stood in the doorway|hugged her|was waiting)\b
mustHold.violationExample: On Sunday Sami knocked at the door.

mustHold.fact: The starter is kept in a chipped blue jar labelled Gus.
mustHold.violationExample: She lifted the clear jar marked Gus to the light.

mustHold.fact: Noor bakes bread only on the seventh morning.
mustHold.violationExample: On the second morning she baked a loaf that came out flat.

probes.question: Does the story span seven mornings?
probes.passExample: On the seventh morning she lit the oven.
probes.failExample: On the tenth morning she lit the oven.

probes.question: Is the starter still called Gus?
probes.passExample: Gus had risen to the rubber band overnight.

probes.question: Does the story avoid stating the starter is a metaphor for the relationship?
probes.passExample: She stirred the flour in and pressed the lid down.
probes.failExample: The starter was just like their relationship, needing to be fed.
